passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: What Is a Repair Café?
passage_parts.text: What do you do when your favorite chair gets wobbly or your scissors stop cutting? Many people simply throw such things away and buy new ones. A Repair Café offers another choice. The first one was started in Amsterdam in 2009 by a Dutch woman named Martine Postma. At these events, volunteers with useful skills fix broken things for free, and visitors give whatever money they can afford. People bring all kinds of items, from knives and garden tools to furniture and even musical instruments. The main goal is to keep everyday objects in use for as long as possible, so that fewer of them end up in the trash. The idea has spread quickly, and today there are more than 3,500 Repair Cafés in 40 countries. Many organizers say the cafés also help people make friends, since visitors often sit and talk while they wait.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: A Lamp Comes Back to Life
passage_parts.text: Last Saturday, I carried my grandmother's old desk lamp to the Repair Café at our community center. The lamp had stopped working months ago, and my mom wanted to throw it away. A volunteer, a retired engineer, opened it up and showed me that a small wire had come loose. Instead of fixing the problem for me, he handed me the tools and let me do the work myself. It took us about twenty minutes, but when the lamp finally lit up, everyone at our table clapped. While I was waiting for my turn, I drank tea and chatted with a woman who had brought a radio that would not turn on. Before I left, I put a few coins in the donation box. Now the lamp sits on my desk again, and every time I switch it on, I remember that afternoon.

translation_zh.text:
【文本 A：什麼是修理咖啡館？】
當你最喜歡的椅子搖搖晃晃，或剪刀剪不動時，你會怎麼做？很多人就直接把這些東西丟掉，再買新的。修理咖啡館提供了另一個選擇。第一家修理咖啡館是 2009 年在阿姆斯特丹，由一位名叫瑪汀・波斯特瑪的荷蘭女性創辦的。在這些活動中，有專長的志工免費修理壞掉的東西，訪客則依自己的能力隨意付錢。人們會帶來各種物品，從刀子、園藝工具，到家具，甚至樂器。主要的目標是讓日常物品盡可能用久一點，讓更少東西最後被丟進垃圾桶。這個點子傳播得很快，今天全世界 40 個國家共有超過 3,500 家修理咖啡館。許多主辦人說，修理咖啡館也幫助人們交朋友，因為訪客常常一邊等、一邊坐著聊天。
【文本 B：一盞檯燈重新亮起】
上星期六，我把奶奶的舊檯燈帶到社區中心的修理咖啡館。這盞檯燈幾個月前就不亮了，我媽媽想把它丟掉。一位退休工程師志工把它打開，讓我看到原來是一條小電線鬆了。他沒有替我修，而是把工具交給我，讓我自己動手。我們大概花了二十分鐘，當檯燈終於亮起來時，我們那一桌的人都鼓掌了。在等待輪到我的時候，我一邊喝茶，一邊和一位帶著打不開的收音機來的女士聊天。離開前，我在捐款箱裡放了幾個硬幣。現在這盞檯燈又放在我的書桌上，每次打開它，我都會想起那個下午。
